Root cause:

findings.claim: Every thumbnail render blocks on the remote Google Fonts stylesheet (FONTS_LINK in theme.ts:4) because setContent waits for 'load'. On a stalled network (captive portal, conference wifi, proxy blackhole) each render waits the full 15s RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS and then throws, so the single-worker queue takes N×15s and produces no thumbnails. The comment in theme.ts:3 claims rendering falls back to system fonts, but with a stalled connection it fails instead. A fast DNS failure does fall back, and the cache key has no font state, so a fallback-font PNG stays cached for good.
findings.repro: Verified. Playwright context with javaScriptEnabled:false and route('https://fonts.googleapis.com/**', () => {}) (never answered); page.setContent('<link rel=stylesheet href=https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo>…', {waitUntil:'load', timeout:3000}) throws 'Timeout 3000ms exceeded'. In the app, point fonts.googleapis.com at 10.255.255.1 in /etc/hosts, open a 20-slide deck: about 5 minutes of timeouts, every thumb fails with agent.error.

findings.claim: Every deck.changed (even a one-field PATCH on one slide) makes each open client re-run the whole reload: GET /api/deck, GET /api/versions, then N sequential /api/thumbs/for calls. Server-side, each of those calls re-reads the slide JSON, re-assembles the HTML, and re-reads and SHA-256s the full bytes of every asset the slide lists (thumbs.ts:151-168). Nothing memoizes asset hashes by mtime/size, so one edit costs O(slides × asset bytes) disk reads and hashing per client.
findings.repro: Import the SF deck (pnpm import:sf) and open 2 browser tabs. Run curl -X PATCH localhost:4177/api/slides/<id> -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":"x"}'. The server log/fs trace (e.g. `sudo fs_usage -f filesys node | grep assets`) shows every asset file read twice per slide per tab, although only one slide changed.

findings.claim: When a thumb is not cached, the route hashes the slide (reading all asset bytes) through thumbHash, then calls thumbs.thumb(slide), which re-assembles the HTML and hashes every asset again (thumbs.ts:108-109). Asset I/O and hashing run twice per cache miss.
findings.repro: Add a counter to readFile in ThumbService.hashFor. Request GET /api/thumbs/for/<id> for an uncached slide with one asset: the asset is read twice before the screenshot, plus once more by serveAsset.

findings.claim: The render queue has no bound and no supersession. Each intermediate content hash of a slide edited in quick succession enqueues its own Chromium render, and stale ones are never cancelled, so the thumb for the current content waits behind every obsolete render. The inflight dedupe in routes/thumbs.ts only collapses identical hashes.
findings.repro: Send 20 PATCH /api/slides/<id> with titles t1..t20 back to back while a tab is open. Each deck.changed triggers /api/thumbs/for/<id> with a new hash, so 20 renders queue and the t20 thumb.ready arrives only after all 19 stale PNGs are rendered and written.

findings.claim: commit() rewrites slides/<id>.json with atomic tmp+rename and runs an exists() check on objects/<hash>.json for every slide in the deck on every commit, then readdirs slides/. A single-slide manual edit costs O(N) file writes and fsyncs instead of O(changed).
findings.repro: On a 30-slide deck, run one PATCH /api/slides/<id>. `ls -l --time-style=full-iso slides/` shows all 30 files with a new mtime.

findings.claim: GET /api/versions/:n reads and zod-parses every versions/v*.json only to check that n exists, although snapshotAt already reads v{n}.json directly. Combined with the client fetching the full /api/versions list on every deck.changed (Main.tsx:31), per-request cost grows linearly with history, and every accept adds a version.
findings.repro: Script 1000 PATCH edits (1000 versions), then time `curl localhost:4177/api/versions/3`. It reads 1000 files. The GET /api/versions that follows each deck.changed also returns and parses all 1000 on every client.

findings.claim: cache/thumbs grows without bound. Every distinct content hash (every intermediate edit, every theme change) leaves a PNG of hundreds of KB, and nothing prunes hashes that no longer belong to main, any version, or any lane.
findings.repro: Run 100 PATCH edits on one slide with a tab open, then `ls cache/thumbs | wc -l`: 100+ PNGs, of which only the latest is referenced by main.

findings.claim: snapshotAt returns the content-addressed object as-is, so any two slides with identical content (duplicate slide, two empty/placeholder slides) come back with the wrong id: slides['s_b'].id === 's_a'. Committing that snapshot (the planned restore path, plan line 375) throws `slide keyed "s_b" carries id "s_a"`, and diff/restore logic keyed on slide.id is wrong. Fix: `slides[id] = { ...obj, id }`.

The M2 lane preview (apply all pending changes) will then fail on a lane that rebase marked healthy.
findings.repro: `rebaseLane({..., changes: [{kind:'remove',slide:'s1',status:'pending'}, {kind:'modify',slide:'s1',patch:{title:'x'},status:'pending'}]}, {order:['s1'], slides:{s1}})` returns statuses `['pending','pending']` (checked).

findings.claim: sanitizeBody strips closing `</script>` in a separate pass that runs after the pair-removal passes, so it can put back a working script element. `<scr</script>ipt>alert(1)</scr</script>ipt>` comes out as `<script>alert(1)</script>`. GET /api/present serves bodies with JS enabled on the app origin (127.0.0.1:4177), so the injected script can call PATCH /api/slides and PUT /api/brief. Slide bodies come from imported HTML, from PATCH /api/slides/:id (which has no validateBody), and from AI lanes in M2. Plan Review Focus 3 requires that scripts never execute.
findings.repro: Call sanitizeBody('<scr</script>ipt>alert(1)</scr</script>ipt>'); it returns "<script>alert(1)</script>" (confirmed with tsx). End to end: curl -X PATCH localhost:4177/api/slides/<id> -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"body":"<scr</script>ipt>alert(document.domain)</scr</script>ipt>"}', then open /present.

findings.claim: The on* attribute stripper only rewrites a tag when the whole attribute list matches its whitespace-separated grammar. If the tag deviates from that grammar, the regex fails and every attribute is kept, including on* handlers. Browsers accept `/` as an attribute separator and accept a quoted value followed directly by the next attribute, so these handlers fire in /api/present.
findings.repro: sanitizeBody('') and sanitizeBody('') both return their input unchanged (confirmed with tsx). PATCH either one into a slide body and open /present: onerror runs on the app origin.

findings.claim: The sanitizer is a denylist of <script> tags and on* attributes. It lets through other script vectors that run with the app origin's privileges in present mode: `<iframe srcdoc>` with an entity-encoded script (a srcdoc frame is same-origin with its parent), `<iframe src="javascript:...">`, `<object data=javascript:...>`, and `<a href=javascript:...>`.
findings.repro: sanitizeBody('<iframe srcdoc="<script>parent.fetch(\'/api/brief\',{method:\'PUT\',headers:{\'content-type\':\'application/json\'},body:\'{}\'})</script>"></iframe>') returns the input unchanged (confirmed for srcdoc and src=javascript:). Loading /present then runs the payload.

findings.claim: slideSection concatenates raw sanitized bodies into a single #viewport. One stray closing tag in any body, such as an unmatched ``, closes #viewport early. Every later slide then falls outside `#viewport>.slide`, and the player skips them without any error. Plan Review Focus 3 requires that an unbalanced tag must not break the stage. Present mode is the one place where a single slide can break the others.
findings.repro:
Assemble three slides whose bodies are '

one

', '

two

', '

three

' as presentRoutes does, then load the page in Chromium: document.querySelectorAll('#viewport>.slide').length is 1, not 3 (confirmed with a Playwright probe).

findings.claim: The direct-edit PATCH writes `body` without calling validateBody. The plan requires that check to reject <script>, <ul>/<ol> and empty bodies, and it is the only barrier in front of the flawed sanitizer. The `assets` entries are also taken as arbitrary strings, for example '../../x' or '/etc/passwd', and stored in the content-addressed objects.
findings.repro:
curl -X PATCH localhost:4177/api/slides/ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"body":"
  • a
","assets":["../../../etc/passwd"]}' returns 200 and commits a new version.

findings.claim: The importer resolves any relative `src` against htmlDir without confining it. A deck.html that contains `` makes the import copy that file into /assets/id_rsa. @fastify/static then serves it at /assets/id_rsa. An untrusted deck file can pull arbitrary local files into the served folder.
findings.repro:
Write /tmp/d/deck.html containing `

x

` and run importDeckHtmlFile('/tmp/d/deck.html', {outDir:'/tmp/out',...}). /tmp/out/assets/hosts now exists, and GET /assets/hosts returns it.

findings.claim: Neither /ws nor the REST routes check the Origin or Host header. Any web page the user visits can open ws://127.0.0.1:4177/ws, since browsers do not apply CORS to WebSockets, and read every bus event, including agent.error messages. A DNS-rebinding page can also reach /api/* and pass PATCH/PUT preflights, because the Host header is not validated.
findings.repro: From any origin, in the devtools console: new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:4177/ws').onmessage=e=>console.log(e.data). Then edit a slide in the app; the deck.changed event arrives at the foreign page.

findings.claim: `pnpm import:sf` runs `rm(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` on decks/dss-sf-2026 without asking or backing anything up. This deletes every version, object, lane, thread and remark the creator has built up. It also bypasses the importer's own 'already holds a deck' guard (fromDeckHtml.ts:103). decks/* is gitignored, so the history cannot be recovered. The CLI error in src/cli/main.ts:20 even tells users to run this command.
findings.repro: pnpm import:sf; pnpm dev decks/dss-sf-2026; curl -X PATCH localhost:4177/api/slides/<id> -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":"x"}' (now v2); pnpm import:sf again. Result: ls decks/dss-sf-2026/versions shows only v0/v1, v2 and the edit are gone, and nothing is printed except 'imported N slides'.

findings.claim: commit() is not crash-consistent. slides/<id>.json is overwritten first (line 191), then versions/v{n}.json is written (194), and only after that is deck.json bumped (195). A crash, kill -9 or ENOSPC between 194 and 195 leaves v{n}.json on disk while deck.json still says n-1. From then on every commit throws 'version n already exists' (line 181), so the deck is stuck and every edit returns 500 until someone deletes the file by hand. A crash before 194 is also bad: main silently shows slide contents from a version that was never recorded.
findings.repro: Simulate the crash window. With deck.json at version 1, create decks/X/versions/v2.json (copy v1.json and set n=2). Then PATCH /api/slides/<id> {"title":"x"}. It returns 500 'version 2 already exists', and every later edit fails the same way.

findings.claim: ThumbService never notices that Chromium has died and never relaunches it. If the browser crashes or is killed (OOM, sleep/wake, a user killing stray Chromium processes), this.page stays set, so every later setContent rejects with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. The server keeps running and serving the UI, but no thumbnail ever renders again until the whole process is restarted. The only trace is one error log line per request.
findings.repro: Start deckstudio on a deck. Run pkill -f 'chrome-headless-shell|Chromium' (the Playwright child). Edit a slide via PATCH /api/slides/<id>. GET /api/thumbs/for/<id> returns ready:false forever, and the server log shows 'thumbnail render failed' with 'Target ... closed' on every retry.

findings.claim: The server reports a failed thumbnail render to clients as `agent.error` on thread 'global'. The log is mislabelled: it says the agent failed when it was the renderer. The web client (web/src/screens/Main.tsx:51-58) ignores agent.error and gets no thumb.ready, so the slide shows the grey title placeholder forever with nothing in the UI saying the render failed. Once the chat thread UI exists in M2, the render failure will show up as an AI error in the global chat.
findings.repro: Put a slide whose body references an asset served slowly, or break rendering (e.g. stop the browser as above). Open the UI: the thumb stays a placeholder with no error indicator. Watching /ws shows {"type":"agent.error","thread":"global","message":"thumbnail render failed for s_..."}.

findings.claim: Every rendered page loads the Google Fonts stylesheet (theme.ts:56, FONTS_LINK), but font availability is not part of the render hash. A thumbnail rendered offline (or when fonts.googleapis.com is slow or blocked) is drawn with fallback system fonts and then cached under the same hash forever. Coming back online never refreshes it. On a slow network, setContent with waitUntil 'load' can also hit the 15s RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS and fail the render entirely.
findings.repro: Disconnect from the network, start deckstudio on a fresh deck and let the thumbs render. Reconnect and reload the UI: the thumbs keep the fallback fonts (same hash, served from cache/thumbs) while /api/present shows Archivo. Only rm -r cache/thumbs fixes it.

findings.claim: When a store is passed, the importer calls store.init(), which writes deck.json at v0, before it copies the assets or commits the slides. If copyFile fails partway (permissions, a file vanishing between the exists check and the copy, ENOSPC), the folder is left marked as a deck but has no slides or only some assets. Re-running the import without the destructive rm then refuses with 'already holds a deck', and the CLI opens a deck with 0 slides and no error.
findings.repro: Make one referenced asset unreadable after the existence check, e.g. chmod 000 on the asset file, then call importDeckHtmlFile(path, {outDir, name, brief, store: DeckStore}). It throws EACCES. Now run deckstudio <outDir>: it starts with 'v0 · 0 slides', and a second import throws 'already holds a deck'.

findings.claim: The shutdown handler takes over the default SIGINT behaviour but has no re-entry guard and no forced-exit path. Pressing Ctrl-C while a render is in progress waits for app.close and thumbs.stop, which awaits the render queue for up to 2x15s. A second Ctrl-C just calls shutdown() again (app.close is called twice) instead of force-quitting. Any rejection inside shutdown becomes an unhandled rejection because of `void`.
findings.repro: Start deckstudio on a deck whose slide references a slow remote resource so a render sits near the 15s timeout. Press Ctrl-C twice. The process stays alive until the render times out, with no output.

findings.claim: When the WebSocket reconnects (e.g. after the server restarts under `pnpm dev`, which is tsx watch), the client never calls reload(). Thumb renders that were in flight when the server died never produce a thumb.ready event, and edits made during the gap are missed. The filmstrip keeps showing placeholders or a stale deck until the page is refreshed manually.
findings.repro: Run pnpm dev <deck> with the UI open on a fresh cache. Touch a src file while the thumbs are still rendering so tsx restarts the server. The socket reconnects, but the remaining thumbs stay grey placeholders until the browser is refreshed.

findings.claim: snapshotAt() returns the content-addressed object as stored, and that object's id belongs to whichever slide wrote it first. The id is left out of hashSlide, so two slides with identical content share one object. Their positions in a historical snapshot then come back carrying the wrong id: slides[id].id != id. GET /api/versions/:n returns that corrupted payload. Re-committing the snapshot throws, and restore / open-as-lane in the plan (Task 16) are built on exactly that re-commit. Fix: set slides[id] = { ...obj, id } when reading.
findings.repro: pnpm exec tsx on a script: DeckStore.init(tmp); commit two slides s_a and s_b with the same title/story/notes/body/assets/kind; snapshotAt(1) gives 's_b -> s_a'; store.commit(snapshotAt(1), {kind:'restore',...}) throws 'slide keyed "s_b" carries id "s_a"' (verified).

findings.claim: ThumbService resolves each Slide.assets entry relative to assetsDir. The importer, following decisions.md ('Slide.assets stores ... "assets/<basename>"'), stores 'assets/s02.png', so the path resolves to <deck>/assets/assets/s02.png. That file never exists, and the thumb hash takes the 'missing' branch for every imported asset. Replacing an asset's bytes therefore never invalidates the cached thumbnail, which contradicts the stated cache contract. Tests pass only because the thumbs test uses a bare name ('s02.png') that the importer never produces.
findings.repro: Import tests/fixtures/deck-3.html with store: DeckStore. Compute ThumbService.thumbHash(slide0), overwrite <deck>/assets/s02.png with different bytes, and compute thumbHash again. The two hashes are identical (verified: 'SAME hash after asset bytes changed').

findings.claim: The plan's Review Focus 3 says the renderer must not execute scripts. sanitizeBody strips only literal <script> tags and on* attributes. The present player (/api/present) runs with JavaScript on and uses this same sanitization, so these bodies still execute there: <iframe srcdoc="<script>..."> (entity-encoded script, runs same-origin), javascript: hrefs, and <object data=...>. validateBody, the gate for AI-proposed bodies, also accepts them.
findings.repro: sanitizeBody('x') returns the input unchanged, and validateBody on it returns {ok:true} (verified). To reproduce end to end: PATCH /api/slides/ with that body, then open /api/present; the alert fires in the parent page.

findings.claim: The plan's exact interface is importDeckHtml({html, htmlDir, outDir, name, brief}), with no store. Called that way, the importer writes deck.json with version 1 but creates no versions/v1.json, objects/, lanes/, threads/, cache/thumbs/ or remarks.json, which breaks the spec's storage layout. DeckStore.open accepts the folder, but versions() fails with ENOENT, so GET /api/versions returns 500, and snapshotAt(1) and lanes() fail as well.
findings.repro: Call importDeckHtml({html: deck-3.html, htmlDir: tests/fixtures, outDir: tmp, name, brief}) without store, then (await DeckStore.open(tmp)).versions(). It throws 'ENOENT: scandir .../versions' (verified).

findings.claim: init() writes an empty v0 with cause 'import', and the importer then commits v1, also with cause 'import'. Every imported deck therefore has two 'import' versions, the first with zero slides. The version line shows v0 as an empty import, and VersionLine's empty-state copy ('Importing a deck creates v0') is wrong. Under the spec, a version should be a state of main created by an acceptance or the import, not a phantom empty deck.
findings.repro: pnpm import:sf, or import deck-3.html with store: DeckStore, then store.versions() returns ['0:import:0 slides', '1:import:3 slides'] (verified). GET /api/versions shows both.
